scope: Proposition 5.3 of the manuscript “The abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture” (preprints/The-Abelian-Zilber-Pink-Conjecture-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 53e8f20495ac6168), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a minimal admissible choice, the following assertions hold after discarding finitely many indices and passing to a subsequence. 1. For every pair of positive integers D, B, there is an index i0(D, B) such that, for every i ≥ i0(D, B) and every factor ℓ, any hypersurface of degree at most D defined over an extension Fi/ki with [Fi : ki] ≤ B which contains yiℓ also contains Ziℓ. 2. For each fixed degree, the equations of Ziℓ in that degree have a ki-basis of coefficient heights O(Hiℓ). The points yiℓ are smooth on Ziℓ, and equations of bounded degree and height O(Hiℓ) span their conormal spaces. 3. The low factor belongs to a finite set of varieties. We may therefore suppose Zi0 = Z0 independent of i.
